approved_translation: Self-sacrifice for the sake of others is the highest virtue; compassion moves even kings.
translation_author: Ellen C. Babbitt (retold from traditional sources)
context_summary: There was once a Deer the color of gold. His eyes were like round jewels, his horns were white as silver, his mouth was red like a flower, his hoofs were bright and hard. I grant your life and hers. Nor will I hunt any more the Deer in either park or forest."
interpretation_boundaries: Do not depict specific historical Buddha figures — keep characters as generic animals or people
Focus on the moral lesson, avoid doctrinal Buddhist claims
Keep animal characters naturalistic, not anthropomorphic
